Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anastácio M, Marreilha dos Santos AP, Aschner M, Mateus L · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Determination of trace metals in fruit juices in the Portuguese market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 434-439</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Across 2 other studies of ordinary farms and markets, reported lead means and medians on an as-sold or fresh-weight basis ranged from 2 µg/kg (Alzagtat et al. 2016) to 7 µg/kg (Alzagtat et al. 2016).<sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Alzagtat et al. 2016 reported cadmium at 5 µg/kg (mean ± 3 SD) and total arsenic at 40 µg/kg (mean ± 5 SD) in orange juice, juice from imported nectar, producer code E (sample 15).<sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the orange juice came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-orange-juice" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-orange-juice-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of orange juice, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:orange-juice-0020cf6b4a16:3b40255140ac"><summary>HMI orange juice Pb reference · Orange juice, juice</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:orange-juice-0020cf6b4a16:3b40255140ac"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI orange juice Pb reference · Orange juice, juice. Orange juice, juice; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤1</td><td>≤1</td><td>0.2–4 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤1</td><td>≤1</td><td>0.2–4 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>71 reference units; 4 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>45</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>Spungen et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2018</td><td>22</td><td>25%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for orange juice, juice on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>4 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li><li><a href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" class="internal" data-slug="sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" data-no-cite-meta>Spungen et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018" data-no-cite-meta>U.S. Food and Drug Administration 2018</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:orange-juice-0020cf6b4a16:3b40255140ac</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Song et al. 2024 is the only compatible sampling family for orange juice, juice on this basis in the completed orange juice ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Orange juice FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-orange-juice" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-orange-juice" data-question="What heavy metals are found in orange juice?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in orange juice?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn and CrVI in orange juice, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anastácio M, Marreilha dos Santos AP, Aschner M, Mateus L · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Determination of trace metals in fruit juices in the Portuguese market</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports 5 (2018) 434-439</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/anastacio2018-portugal-fruit-juices-trace-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in orange juice, juice from 183 results in 4 reporting regions, with a subgroup median of 6.6 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-orange-juice-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-orange-juice-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of orange juice measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of orange juice measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 22 groups of orange juice ranged from 0.1 µg/kg (FY2017) to 21.7 µg/kg (FY2018); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Analytical Results for Lead in Juice Sampled Under the FDA&#39;s Toxic Elements in Food and Foodware, and Radionuclides in Food – Import and Domestic Compliance Program (FY2005-FY2018)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA analytical results table</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2018-lead-in-juice-fy2005-fy2018">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 7 groups of orange juice ranged from 2 µg/kg (imported nectar, producer code F (sample 16)) to 7 µg/kg (locally produced nectar, producer code A (sample 13)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alzagtat AA, Eledody RY · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Conformity of Fruit Nectar Samples to Libyan Specification Standards</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/alzagtat2016-fruit-nectars-libya-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
